title: Optimize control-plane query hotpaths, remove unused FK columns, and add covering indexes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We have several recurring P95 latency spikes and sustained CPU burn in the control-plane Postgres cluster caused by a small set of slow queries over policy/tenant/join tables. This ticket bundles a safe refactor and schema cleanup plan: remove legacy FK columns left from the multi-tenant migration, add targeted covering indexes to the hot SELECT paths, rewrite two queries to use EXISTS instead of broad JOINs, and land zero-downtime migrations with a guarded feature flag.

Goals:
- Reduce median and P95 read latency on control-plane queries that serve route lookup and permission checks (target: 40% P95 reduction).
- Remove 2 legacy FK columns (tenant_legacy_id, policy_hash_v1) that increase row width and complicate indexes.
- Create 3 covering indexes to eliminate TL;DR sequential scans on policy_rules and tenant_mappings.
- Ensure all changes are reversible with a rollback migration and gating via a runtime flag.

Scope of work:
1) Query analysis & benchmarks (done): collected top 25 slow queries via pg_stat_statements and trace sampling; identified 4 queries that account for ~55% of PG CPU in control-plane. Captured EXPLAIN ANALYZE baselines and a representative 10k-request replay set.
2) Schema migrations (planned): add new partial/covering indexes concurrently; deploy dual-write for one shortened FK column, backfill; drop legacy columns in a later change window after monitoring. Use PG concurrent index creation and synchronous backfill scripts.
3) Query rewrites (in progress): change two codepaths in control-plane service: route-lookup and policy-eval. Replace multi-join patterns with EXISTS and indexed lookups, and introduce LIMIT 1 guards where semantics allow.
4) Observability & rollback: extend console trace dashboards, add alerting for index bloat and long-running create index ops, and include automatic revert migration scripts.

Risks & mitigations:
- Long-running CREATE INDEX: use CONCURRENTLY and schedule low-traffic window; monitor lock stats; have pg_cancel_backend playbook ready.
- Unexpected plan regression: deploy rewrites behind feature flag and run 10k-request replay in staging; promote to prod only after P95 improvements verified.
- Backfill or dual-write mismatch: use checksum compare jobs and data-verification runbooks before dropping columns.

Acceptance criteria:
- P95 latency for the route-lookup and policy-eval endpoints reduced by >=30% in production within one week of rollout.
- Legacy columns removed and table sizes reduced (storage savings reported).
- No data correctness regressions observed; migration rollback tested in staging and runbook validated.
